title: Package the existing React frontend as a signed Android APK (Capacitor) with Internet Identity compatibility

requirements.summary: Add an Android app wrapper project alongside the React frontend to build debug and signed release APKs.
acceptanceCriteria: Repository contains Android wrapper project/config committed alongside the existing frontend.
A developer can run documented commands to generate a debug APK locally.
A developer can generate a release APK (signed) using documented environment variables/keystore inputs without modifying source code.

file_operations.description: Add Capacitor configuration for the existing React build output (appId, appName, webDir, server/allowNavigation as needed for Internet Identity).
Commit Android wrapper Gradle properties suitable for local builds (no secrets committed).
Commit the top-level Android wrapper Gradle configuration generated for the Capacitor Android project.
Commit the Android app module Gradle configuration, including debug/release buildTypes and signing config that can be driven by environment variables/CI inputs (without source edits).

Add Android manifest configuration required for network access and Capacitor WebView hosting (e.g., INTERNET permission) and any required intent filters for auth return (only what is strictly necessary).
Add/commit the Capacitor MainActivity for the Android wrapper (as generated), ensuring it loads the Capacitor-hosted web app.
Add a network security config file if needed for local development/test environments (avoid weakening production settings).
Adjust the HTML metadata if needed for Capacitor Android (e.g., ensure viewport and base assumptions work correctly in WebView) while keeping the existing React entry intact.

requirements.summary: Ensure Internet Identity login/logout works reliably in the Android WebView context without modifying immutable Internet Identity hook files.
acceptanceCriteria: User can log in and log out successfully on Android build (no blank window / blocked popup during login).
No edits are made to any immutable paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT (including frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts and frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts).

file_operations.description: Add a small helper to detect when the app is running under a Capacitor Android WebView (used to switch authentication flow behavior).

Add an Internet Identity WebView compatibility shim that, when running in Capacitor, routes login window creation to an external browser/custom tab and returns focus to the app. This must not require any edits to immutable hook files.
Initialize the Internet Identity WebView compatibility shim early in app runtime (before the user can tap Login), without changing any immutable hook files.

Update the login button behavior to use the Android-compatible login flow when running in Capacitor (e.g., trigger external browser flow and handle return), while continuing to call the existing immutable useInternetIdentity login/clear functions.

Add/adjust the minimal Android intent handling required for returning from the external browser/custom tab back into the app during Internet Identity login (only what is strictly necessary; no extra deep linking features).

requirements.summary: Add concise repository documentation for prerequisites and commands to build debug and signed release APKs.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation includes required tooling (Android Studio/SDK/Java version) and exact commands to build.
Documentation includes configuration steps for release signing and where the resulting APK outputs are located.

file_operations.description: Document prerequisites (Android Studio/SDK, Java version), one-time setup, and exact commands to build debug and release APKs, including Capacitor sync steps and where APK artifacts are produced.
Add release signing guidance describing how to provide keystore materials via environment variables/CI secrets (do not commit keystores), and how the Android Gradle signing config reads these inputs.
Ensure the release signing configuration is driven by documented environment variables/keystore inputs (no source modifications required to switch between debug and release signing).
